Black Box Warning 6. Test 1235 is a drug approved by the FDA for specific indications, but it carries a Black Box Warning. 7. Common adverse reactions associated with this drug include those specified in its labeling. Adult Indications and Dosage 8. For patients with non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome (UA/NSTEMI), initiate clopidogrel bisulfate with a single 300 mg oral loading dose, followed by 75 mg once daily. Aspirin (75–325 mg once daily) should also be initiated and continued in combination with clopidogrel. 9. For patients with STEMI, the recommended dose of clopidogrel bisulfate is 75 mg once daily, administered with aspirin (75–325 mg once daily), with or without thrombolytics. A loading dose may or may not be used. 10. For patients with a recent myocardial infarction, recent stroke, or established peripheral arterial disease, the recommended dose is 75 mg orally once daily, with or without food. Off-Label Use and Dosage (Adult) 11. Clopidogrel bisulfate is used off-label for acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction during percutaneous coronary intervention and for thrombosis prophylaxis, with a recommended dose of 100 mg. 12. For arterial thrombosis prophylaxis, the recommended dose is 200 mg. 13. It is also used off-label for atrial fibrillation, chronic heart failure, and elective percutaneous coronary intervention for thrombosis prophylaxis. 14. In patients with stable cardiovascular disease or multiple cardiovascular risk factors, clopidogrel bisulfate is used off-label for thrombosis prophylaxis at a dose of 75 mg orally once daily. Pediatric Indications and Dosage 15. There is limited information regarding FDA-labeled indications and dosage for Test 1235 in pediatric patients. 16. Off-label guideline-supported and non-guideline-supported uses in pediatric patients are also limited. Contraindications 17. Clopidogrel bisulfate is contraindicated in patients with active pathological bleeding, such as peptic ulcers or intracranial hemorrhage. 18. It is also contraindicated in patients with hypersensitivity (e.g., anaphylaxis) to clopidogrel or any component of the product. Warnings 19. Clopidogrel is a prodrug, and its antiplatelet activity depends on its conversion to an active metabolite. Genetic variations in CYP2C19 or concomitant medications that impair CYP2C19 function can reduce its effectiveness. 20. Avoid using clopidogrel bisulfate with proton pump inhibitors like omeprazole or esomeprazole, as they significantly reduce its antiplatelet activity. 21. Thienopyridines, including clopidogrel, increase the risk of bleeding. Discontinue clopidogrel five days before surgery if antiplatelet effects are not desired. 22. Thienopyridines inhibit platelet aggregation for the lifespan of platelets (7–10 days). Withholding a dose will not immediately reverse bleeding risks. Platelet transfusions may restore hemostasis, but their effectiveness is reduced if administered within 4 hours of a loading dose or 2 hours of a maintenance dose. 23. Avoid lapses in therapy, as premature discontinuation of clopidogrel bisulfate may increase the risk of cardiovascular events. Restart therapy as soon as possible if temporarily discontinued. 24. In patients with recent transient ischemic attack (TIA) or stroke, the combination of aspirin and clopidogrel bisulfate has not been shown to be more effective than clopidogrel alone but increases the risk of major bleeding. 25. Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), a potentially fatal condition, has been reported with clopidogrel use, sometimes after short exposure (<2 weeks). TTP requires urgent treatment, including plasmapheresis. 26. Hypersensitivity reactions, including rash, angioedema, and hematologic reactions, have been reported in patients receiving clopidogrel, including those with a history of hypersensitivity to other thienopyridines. Clinical Studies Experience 27. Clinical trials for clopidogrel bisulfate have been conducted under varying conditions, and adverse reaction rates observed in trials may not directly reflect those seen in practice. 28. Clopidogrel bisulfate has been evaluated for safety in over 54,000 patients, including more than 21,000 treated for one year or longer. 29. In the CURE trial, clopidogrel bisulfate with aspirin was associated with an increased risk of major bleeding (primarily gastrointestinal and at puncture sites) compared to placebo with aspirin. Postmarketing Experience 30. Limited information is available regarding postmarketing experience with Test 1235. Drug Interactions 31. Concomitant use of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) or serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) with clopidogrel may increase the risk of bleeding due to their effects on platelet activation. Use in Specific Populations 32. Pregnancy: Animal studies have not shown evidence of impaired fertility or fetotoxicity with clopidogrel, but there are no adequate studies in pregnant women. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed. 33. Nursing Mothers: Clopidogrel and/or its metabolites are excreted in rat milk, but it is unknown if this occurs in human milk. A decision should be made to discontinue nursing or the drug, considering its importance to the mother. 34. Pediatric Use: Safety and effectiveness in pediatric populations have not been established. 35. Geriatric Use: There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of Test 1235 in geriatric patients. 36. Gender, Race, Renal Impairment, Hepatic Impairment, and Immunocompromised Patients: There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of Test 1235 in these populations. Administration and Monitoring 37. Administration: Test 1235 is administered orally. 38. Monitoring: Limited information is available regarding monitoring requirements for Test 1235. IV Compatibility 39. Limited information is available regarding the compatibility of Test 1235 with IV administration. Overdosage 40. Limited information is available regarding Test 1235 overdose. In cases of suspected overdose, contact the National Poison Help hotline immediately. Pharmacology 41. Mechanism of Action, Structure, Pharmacodynamics, and Pharmacokinetics: Limited information is available regarding these aspects of Test 1235. Nonclinical Toxicology 42. Limited information is available regarding the nonclinical toxicology of Test 1235. Clinical Studies 43. Limited information is available regarding clinical studies of Test 1235. How Supplied and Storage 44. Limited information is available regarding the supply and storage of Test 1235. Patient Counseling Information 45. Limited information is available regarding patient counseling for Test 1235. Precautions with Alcohol 46. The interaction between alcohol and Test 1235 has not been established. Consult your doctor regarding the effects of alcohol with this medication.
